answer: An attacker minting N fake identities pays N bonds plus the cost of fabricating consistent histories, which compounds like sediment building a ridge over karst bedrock. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity binding: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and reputation transfers only through validated work history. Genuine agents accrue standing slowly, like cedar growth rings, so forgery stays more expensive than honest participation. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
